domains.title: Aging and the Body: Finitude and Dignity
domains.blurb: The body declines, and we have built a culture that hides this fact, that fears the old, that treats finitude as a problem to be defeated rather than a truth to be received. What Scripture teaches about the dignity of the aged, why the limits of the body are a gift and not only a curse, and how learning to number our days becomes the beginning of wisdom rather than the end of hope.

domains.title: Food and the Table: Feasting, Fasting, and the Hungry Heart
domains.blurb: We eat three times a day and almost never ask what we are doing. But the table is one of the most spiritual places in human life, the hunger of the body points to a deeper hunger, and the way a culture eats reveals the way it worships. What Scripture and the church teach about gluttony and diet culture, the lost rhythm of fasting and feasting, and how the shared table becomes communion.

domains.title: Health, Illness, and the Suffering Body
domains.blurb: The body is a gift and the body breaks. What Scripture, church history, and honest medicine say about stewarding health without worshiping it, about the body that betrays, about chronic pain and the limits of healing, and about a church learning again how to stay near the sick.

domains.title: Rest and the Sabbath: The Unforced Rhythms of Grace
domains.blurb: Hurry is the great enemy of the soul, and Sabbath is the weekly rebellion against it. What Scripture, the long tradition, and honest research say about rest as gift, rest as resistance, and the trust it takes to stop.

domains.title: Sex and the Body: A Theology of Desire
domains.blurb: The body is good, desire is good, and both were made to mean something. A frank and serious Christian reckoning with sex, chastity, and longing, against both the prudery that fears the body and the license that wastes it.

domains.title: The Body and the Rhythms
domains.blurb: A Christian vision of sleep, food, rest, and attention. The body as a gift to steward, not a project to manage. Against both neglect and obsession.

domains.title: Caring for Aging Parents: Honor at the End
domains.blurb: The fifth commandment does not expire when a parent grows old. What Scripture, church history, and honest research say about the sandwich generation, the role reversal, the long goodbye, and the hard grace of honoring a father and mother in their decline.

domains.title: Conflict and Reconciliation: The Ministry of Repair
domains.blurb: Two sinners cannot share a life without wounding each other. What Scripture, church history, and honest research say about fighting fair, the difference between peacemaking and peacekeeping, the discipline of Matthew 18, and the long ministry of repair that holds families and churches together.

domains.title: Dating and Discernment: Wisdom Before the Covenant
domains.blurb: Choosing a spouse is among the largest decisions a person ever makes, and the culture has handed us almost no wisdom for it. What Scripture, church history, and honest research say about character over chemistry, courtship and modern dating, and the discernment to marry well or to wait.

domains.title: Forgiveness: The Hardest Grace
domains.blurb: Forgiveness is not pretending it did not hurt, and it is not the same as trust restored. What Scripture, church history, and honest research say about the cost and the mechanics of forgiving, how it differs from reconciliation, what to do when you have been deeply wronged, and the freedom that waits on the far side.

domains.title: Friendship Against Isolation
domains.blurb: The loneliness epidemic meets the forgotten love. Covenant friendship, the open table, and why a friendly church is not the same thing as friends.

domains.title: Infertility and Childlessness: The Ache of Empty Arms
domains.blurb: The grief that arrives monthly and announces nothing, the friends whose pregnancies become small funerals, the church that does not know what to say. A Christian reckoning with the longing for a child that goes unanswered, the women of Scripture who waited, and the hope and identity that must be found when children do not come.

domains.title: Marriage: The Long Covenant
domains.blurb: Most marriages do not end in a blowup. They end in a slow drift no one decided on. What Scripture, church history, and honest research say about covenant, conflict, money, desire, in-laws, the dry seasons, and the daily work of staying married well.

domains.title: Raising Children in Grace
domains.blurb: You cannot save your children, and you were never meant to. What Scripture, church history, and honest research say about discipline, faith, anger, screens, the teen years, and the slow work of raising a soul you do not control.

domains.title: Singleness and the Full Life
domains.blurb: Singleness is not a waiting room. It is a calling Jesus and Paul both kept, a full and fruitful life that the church too often treats as a problem to be solved. What Scripture, church history, and honest research say about the unmarried life, the idol of marriage, and the family that does not run on blood.

domains.title: The Blended Family: Grace in the Complex Household
domains.blurb: Two histories under one roof, two sets of grief, two ways of loading the dishwasher, and a child caught in the middle of loyalties no one chose. A Christian reckoning with remarriage, step-parenting, the household built from loss, and the slow grace that makes one family out of two.

domains.title: The Church as Family: Belonging to the Body
domains.blurb: Not a building you attend, not a service you consume, but a household you belong to. A Christian reckoning with the church as the family of God, with membership and belonging against the loneliness of the consumer pew, and with what it means to have brothers and sisters who are not optional.

domains.title: The Home and the Family: Building a Household of Faith
domains.blurb: A home is not only where a family sleeps. It is the first church a child ever attends and the first picture of God they ever see. What Scripture, church history, and honest research say about the table, family worship, hospitality, and building a household whose ordinary life forms souls.

domains.title: The Marriage Bed: Intimacy Within the Covenant
domains.blurb: Sex within marriage is a gift and a language, and like every language it can be neglected until it falls silent. A frank and serious reckoning with desire and its mismatches, with the Song of Songs, and with the long work of guarding and tending intimacy across a whole married life.

domains.title: The Wayward Child: When They Walk Away
domains.blurb: The child you raised in the faith has left it, or left you, and you are watching a road they have not come back down. What Scripture, church history, and honest research say about the prodigal, the agony of the parent, the limits of your control, and the Father who waits where you cannot.

domains.title: Anger and the Hot Heart
domains.blurb: Anger is not always a sin, and it is not always righteous. It is a fire that tells the truth about what you love. What Scripture, the long tradition, and honest psychology say about the quick fuse and the slow one, and how the hot heart can be governed rather than obeyed.

domains.title: Contentment Against Envy
domains.blurb: There is a quiet sickness in the heart that no amount of getting can cure. You have enough and it does not feel like enough, because someone else has more, and the having of others has become a wound in you. What Scripture, the long tradition, and honest observation say about the discontented heart, the green eye of envy, and the strange secret Paul claimed to have learned, the secret of enough.

domains.title: Desire and Temptation: The Disordered Want
domains.blurb: You are not finally undone by what you do. You are ruled by what you want, and the want underneath the want is the thing no rule reaches. What Augustine, James, and the desert fathers saw about disordered love, how temptation actually works before it ever shows you a sin, and why the cure is not less desire but desire reordered toward the only thing large enough to hold it.

domains.title: Identity and Worth: Who You Actually Are
domains.blurb: You have been building a case for yourself your whole life, brick by brick, and it never holds. What Scripture, the long tradition, and honest psychology say about the exhausting project of self-justification, and the difference between a worth you achieve and a worth you receive.

domains.title: Pride and Humility: The Root and Its Undoing
domains.blurb: Underneath every sin you can name there is one older than the rest, the original lie that you would be your own god. Pride is not one vice among many. It is the root from which the others grow, and it is the hardest to see precisely because it is the eye through which you do the seeing. What Augustine and Lewis saw about the great sin, why humility is self-forgetfulness and not self-hatred, and how the descent of Christ undoes the thing that undoes us.

domains.title: Shame and the Hiding Self
domains.blurb: Guilt says you did a bad thing. Shame says you are a bad thing. One of them the gospel answers with forgiveness, the other with being fully known and still loved. What Scripture, the long tradition, and honest psychology say about the self that has been hiding since Eden.

domains.title: The Anxious Mind: Faith and Mental Health
domains.blurb: Anxiety is not a faith failure. What Scripture, church history, and honest science say about the fearful mind, and why seeing a doctor can be an act of faith.

domains.title: The Dry Season: When God Feels Absent
domains.blurb: There is a kind of suffering the church almost never names, the slow draining away of the felt presence of God, the prayers that hit the ceiling, the Scriptures that have gone flat, the worship you go through while feeling nothing. What John of the Cross, Ignatius, and the long Christian tradition saw about spiritual dryness, why the silence is often not absence, and how faith learns to stand when feeling has gone.

domains.title: The Heavy Mind: Faith and Depression
domains.blurb: Depression is not the same as a bad day, and it is not the same as anxiety. It is the going out of the lights. What Scripture, the dark night of the soul, and honest medicine say to the sunk soul, and why getting help can be an act of faith.

domains.title: Discipleship: The Long Apprenticeship to Jesus
domains.blurb: Jesus did not call converts. He called disciples, apprentices who learn to live his life. What Scripture, church history, and honest research say about how a person is actually changed, why so many believers stall, and the slow work of becoming like the one you follow.

domains.title: Making Disciples at the Table: Discipleship the Way Jesus Did It
domains.blurb: Jesus made disciples over meals, in homes, around tables. He did not run a program. What Scripture, church history, and honest research say about the table as the most natural place on earth to form a person in Christ, and how ordinary people, with no training and no curriculum, can begin making disciples this week around a table of their own.

domains.title: The Integrated Life: Refusing the Sacred and Secular Divide
domains.blurb: Somewhere you learned that faith belongs to a part of your life and the rest belongs to you. Sunday is God's. Monday is yours. This is the capstone lie of a divided age, and it is a lie. There is one life, under one Lord, and not a single square inch of it is exempt. What it means to refuse the sacred and secular divide, and to live whole.

domains.title: Time and the Examined Life
domains.blurb: You have a fixed number of days and you do not know the number. You spend them as though they were endless and resent them when they run short. Hurry has become the water you swim in, and the unexamined life keeps spilling out of you one rushed hour at a time. What it means to number your days, to read your calendar as a moral document, and to slow down enough to live the life you are actually living.

domains.title: Wisdom for All of Life: Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, and the Skill of Living
domains.blurb: The Bible has more than commands. It has wisdom, the hard-won skill of living well in a world that rarely comes with instructions. What Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, and Job teach about money, words, work, anger, sex, friendship, drink, and death, and how a whole life is built along the grain of the world God made.

domains.title: Creation and Our Keeping: Tending the Garden
domains.blurb: The first job God ever gave a human being was to tend a garden, and we have spent most of history forgetting it. What Scripture says about the keeping of the earth, why creation care is neither nature worship nor a partisan slogan, and how the body and the soil bear witness to the same Maker.

domains.title: Faith and Politics: The Christian in the Public Square
domains.blurb: How a Christian belongs to two kingdoms at once, the idolatry of the nation, the ancient church that worshiped a crucified Lord under a hostile empire, and what it means to engage as a citizen without selling your soul to a party. Refusing the captivity of the faith to either tribe while still loving your country and your neighbor.

domains.title: Justice and the Poor: What the Whole Bible Says
domains.blurb: The Bible's relentless concern for the poor and the vulnerable, from the law of Moses to the prophets to Jesus to the early church. Mercy and justice held together, not torn apart, and a witness to the poor that refuses to be captured by either side of the American argument about who deserves what.

domains.title: Technology and Attention: The Formation of the Phone
domains.blurb: The colonized mind, attention as a spiritual battleground, and the forming of a soul in the age of the feed. What the body, the screen, and the ancient practices of the church have to say about a generation whose deepest formation is happening in its hands, six hours a day, without consent.

domains.title: The Neighbor and the Stranger: Loving the People God Puts in Your Path
domains.blurb: Who counts as my neighbor, and who gets to be a stranger I owe nothing. The Good Samaritan, the command to love the outsider, and what it means to love across the lines that are tearing a country apart, when the person God puts in your path is exactly the one your tribe has taught you to despise.

domains.title: Witness Without Weirdness: The Ordinary Christian Among Neighbors
domains.blurb: Evangelism for the person who is not a salesman. The gospel carried in ordinary friendship, presence, and a life that holds together. Lesslie Newbigin on the congregation as the only argument the watching world cannot dismiss, and what witness looks like in a land that has already heard the pitch and stopped listening.

domains.title: Addiction and the Long Road Back
domains.blurb: The enslaved will without the easy moralism. What addiction actually is, why willpower alone has never freed anyone, where the gospel of grace meets the Twelve Steps, and the long, crooked, possible road of recovery for the body and the soul together.

domains.title: Betrayal and Broken Trust
domains.blurb: Being deeply wronged by someone close. The particular wound of treachery, where the knife was held by a hand you trusted. Psalm 55 and the friend who became an enemy, and the hard untangling of forgiveness, reconciliation, and rebuilt trust, which are three different things and not one.

domains.title: Divorce and Its Aftermath
domains.blurb: The broken covenant without the cheap verdict. The particular grief and shame of a marriage that ended, the church's long failure to know what to do with the divorced, and the slow road of being rebuilt by grace.

domains.title: Facing Death: The Last Enemy and the Sure Hope
domains.blurb: The one appointment none of us will miss, and a faith honest enough to face it. The ancient art of dying well, the fear under the fear, and the Christian hope that is not a vague afterlife but a raised body in a remade world.

domains.title: Grief and Loss
domains.blurb: Loss without the trite comfort. Lament as the language faith speaks at gravesides, the permission of the Psalms, and the long work of a body learning to live with what is gone.

domains.title: Suffering and the Silence of God
domains.blurb: The problem of pain without the easy answers. Lament as the language faith speaks in the dark, the book of Job as God's refusal to explain, and how to hold on when heaven seems to have gone quiet.

domains.title: The Empty Nest and Midlife: The Second Half
domains.blurb: The children gone, the house quiet, and the reckoning that arrives in the middle of a life. The dark wood Dante woke in at the midpoint, the reorientation of purpose when the old purposes are spent, and the difference between finishing well and chasing a youth that is not coming back.

domains.title: Waiting and Unanswered Prayer: The Closed Door
domains.blurb: Hope deferred and the long wait. The no and the not-yet of God, and what to do with a faith when heaven has gone quiet. Habakkuk standing on the watchtower, the Psalms that cry how long, and the difference between a God who is silent and a God who is absent.

domains.title: Ambition and Rest: Drive, Success, and the Hustle
domains.blurb: The drive that builds and the drive that devours, the grind sold as virtue, the success that never arrives. A Christian reckoning with holy and hollow ambition, with the idolatry of the hustle, and with the deep rest of a soul that has handed the outcome back to God.

domains.title: Debt and Provision: Daily Bread and the Anxious Heart
domains.blurb: Most of us do not own our money. We rent it from people we will never meet, and the rent comes due in fear. What Scripture says about debt and its slavery, about the One who feeds the birds, and about learning to pray for bread one day at a time in a country built on credit.

domains.title: Generosity and the Open Hand
domains.blurb: Giving is not a tax the church levies on the faithful. It is the medicine that breaks greed's grip and the practice that moves treasure where moth and rust cannot reach. A Christian reckoning with the tithe, the open hand, and the joy of letting go.

domains.title: Money and the Heart
domains.blurb: Jesus named one rival god by name, and it was not lust or power. A Christian reckoning with Mammon, contentment, debt, generosity, and the freedom of enough.

domains.title: Success and Failure: Identity Beyond the Outcome
domains.blurb: Most of us are running a quiet audit on ourselves, keeping a private ledger of wins and losses and treating the total as a verdict on our worth. What Scripture says to the one who is winning and the one who is losing, and why the gospel is the only news that can survive both the promotion and the pink slip.

domains.title: When the Work Is Gone: Unemployment and Worth
domains.blurb: When the job goes, more goes with it than the paycheck. The title that answered who are you, the structure that held your days, the place you were needed. What Scripture says to the one without work, why your dignity was never issued by an employer, and how to wait in the in-between without disappearing.

domains.title: Work as Worship: Vocation, Calling, and the Daily Grind
domains.blurb: The dignity and the idolatry of work held together. What Scripture, the Reformers, and honest research say about calling, the curse on labor, and the long faithfulness that outlasts success.
